## Overview

Who shoots best from each zone? I pulled every field-goal attempt from the 2025-26 NBA regular season — 219,160 shots across all 30 teams — and split the half-court into 12 distinct zones. For each zone, the player with the highest FG% (minimum qualifying attempts) is crowned the zone leader and visualized with an animated shot-arc reveal.

The result is a 28-second animation that cycles through all 12 zones, drawing the leader's made shots as neon-green Bézier arcs growing from the shot location to the basket, then retracting before moving to the next zone.

## Zone Design

The half-court is divided into 12 zones — 5 three-point, 4 mid-range, and 3 paint:

```{=html}
<div style="overflow-x:auto;">
<table style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; font-size:0.92em;">
  <thead>
    <tr style="border-bottom:1px solid #444;">
      <th style="text-align:left; padding:6px 12px;">Zone</th>
      <th style="text-align:left; padding:6px 12px;">Type</th>
      <th style="text-align:left; padding:6px 12px;">Definition</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Left Corner 3</td><td>3-point</td><td>x ≤ −220, y ≤ 140</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Left Wing 3</td><td>3-point</td><td>Left side, above the break, angle &lt; −20°</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Top of Key 3</td><td>3-point</td><td>Center, above the break, within ±20°</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Right Wing 3</td><td>3-point</td><td>Right side, above the break, angle &gt; 20°</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Right Corner 3</td><td>3-point</td><td>x ≥ 220, y ≤ 140</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Left Baseline Mid</td><td>Mid-range</td><td>Left of paint, y ≤ 140, inside arc</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Left Elbow Mid</td><td>Mid-range</td><td>Left of paint, y &gt; 140, inside arc</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Right Elbow Mid</td><td>Mid-range</td><td>Right of paint, y &gt; 140, inside arc</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Right Baseline Mid</td><td>Mid-range</td><td>Right of paint, y ≤ 140, inside arc</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Upper Paint</td><td>Paint</td><td>In paint, y &gt; 140 (free-throw lane)</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Paint</td><td>Paint</td><td>In paint, 40 &lt; y ≤ 140 (mid-block)</td></tr>
    <tr><td style="padding:5px 12px;">Restricted Area</td><td>Paint</td><td>In paint, y ≤ 40 (at the rim)</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
</div>
```

Coordinates use the NBA's `ShotChartDetail` system: basket at (0, 0), units in tenths of feet. The 3-point arc has radius 237.5 units (23.75 ft); corners are at x = ±220 (22 ft).

Minimum qualifying attempts vary by zone (75 for 3-point and paint zones; 20–35 for mid-range, which is scarce in the modern NBA).

## How It Works

### 1 — Data collection

Shot data comes from the NBA's `ShotChartDetail` endpoint via `nba_api`. I loop through all 30 teams with `player_id=0` (all players) and a 0.6 s sleep between requests to avoid rate limits. The full dataset is cached as a Parquet file.

```python
from nba_api.stats.endpoints import shotchartdetail

resp = shotchartdetail.ShotChartDetail(
    team_id=team_id,
    player_id=0,
    season_nullable="2025-26",
    season_type_all_star="Regular Season",
    context_measure_simple="FGA",
)
df = resp.get_data_frames()[0]
```

### 2 — Zone assignment

Each shot is assigned a zone by a pure-geometry function using `LOC_X` and `LOC_Y`. Corner 3s are detected first (|x| ≥ 220, y ≤ 140), then above-the-break 3s (distance from rim ≥ 237.5), then paint zones by y-cutoff, then mid-range by side and height.

### 3 — Finding leaders

For each zone, shots are grouped by player, FG% is computed, and the player with the highest FG% above the minimum-attempts threshold is selected.

### 4 — Animation

The animation is built with `matplotlib.animation.FuncAnimation`. Each zone gets a 66-frame slot (~2.2 s at 30 fps):

- **Frames 0–7**: zone highlights, player name and stats appear
- **Frames 8–29**: Bézier arcs grow from shot location → basket
- **Frames 30–43**: full arcs held visible
- **Frames 44–59**: arcs retract basket → shot location
- **Frame 60**: arcs fade, zone dims

The Bézier control point is placed 30% of the shot distance above the straight-line path, making the trajectory read clearly as traveling *into* the rim. The active zone is highlighted by a precomputed RGBA grid rendered with `imshow`.
